entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Churn instead of flare, the impatience or anger turbid and unsettled all through, where *stung* is one sharp point.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pressure made visible, the heat contained but plainly building, hotter than *peeved* and short of the coarseness of *pissed off*.

entries.definition: aroused to impatience or anger
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The state as recoil: something landed, and the impatience or anger is the flinch back from it, where *irritated* only wears on.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Wildness with a threat inside it - the menace is carried by the word itself rather than read in, which is what *untamed* lacks.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The formal counterpart to *feral*, holding the same menace in a stiffer register.

entries.definition: wild and menacing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The heaviest here - the menace lands as ferocity, where *feral* only marks the wildness as dangerous.

entries.definition: partially wild
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a measure of degree - it places something part-way along the scale and judges it not at all.

entries.definition: not subdued or trained for service or use
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Defined against service - neither subdued nor trained to any use, so the wildness is measured by what the thing has not been made to do.

entries.definition: not domesticated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat negation and nothing more, the plainest term in the family, with none of the menace *feral* adds.

entries.definition: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The same natural state as *wild*, but framed as a taming that never happened, so it points at what has not been done to the thing.

entries.definition: in a natural state; not tamed or domesticated or cultivated
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Neutral and broad - it covers the animal, the plant and the uncultivated ground alike, naming the natural state without passing any verdict on it.

entries.definition: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Faults the state for what it does to anyone trying to follow it — unordered, unpredictable and confusing at once, where *wild* only says the reins are off.

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pitches the uncontrolled feeling high enough to suggest the senses have gone with it, which *excited* never implies.
examples: a crowd of delirious baseball fans

entries.definition: completely unordered and unpredictable and confusing
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the same absence of order as *chaotic* but frames it as an order failed rather than an order never present.

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: The unloaded member: it records the uncontrolled excitement and leaves the verdict to whoever is listening.

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Adds hurry and distress to the same uncontrolled feeling, so the energy reads as flailing rather than pleasure.

entries.definition: affected with or marked by frenzy or mania uncontrolled by reason
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reason is overrun rather than loosened, and the word fits both the person seized by the frenzy and the scene that shows it.
examples: the prosecutor's frenzied denunciation of the accused

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and dismissive — it calls the uncontrolled emotion unreason outright instead of merely hinting at it as *delirious* does.

entries.definition: affected with or marked by frenzy or mania uncontrolled by reason
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Gives the same reasonless frenzy a clinical ring, where *frenzied* stays pure motion.
examples: outbursts of drunken violence and manic activity and creativity

entries.definition: marked by uncontrolled excitement or emotion
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The coolest word here, naming the control that is missing rather than picturing the emotion that fills the gap.

entries.definition: not brought under control
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: A flat negative that says only that control was never imposed, so it can read as endurance as easily as excess.

entries.definition: marked by extreme lack of restraint or control
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the extremity of the missing restraint without colouring it, and tips negative only because the gloss calls the lack extreme rather than partial.

entries.definition: very difficult to accept or bear
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The one member that concedes the thing can be accepted or borne, at a price the others say is past paying at all.

entries.definition: (used of persons or their behavior) not acceptable or reasonable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Exasperated rather than judicial - it writes a person or their conduct off as beyond dealing with, where *unacceptable* files a ruling.

entries.definition: too extreme to bear
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the excess itself - the thing has gone past a limit, where *intolerable* simply refuses it without saying by how much.
examples: the insufferable heat of August in a New York apartment with no air conditioning

entries.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat verdict of the three - it rules the thing out rather than measuring what holding it costs, which is what *unbearable* does.

entries.definition: (used of persons or their behavior) not acceptable or reasonable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The cool, formal counterpart of *impossible*: it finds the person or the behaviour unreasonable without any of the heat.

entries.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the weight on whoever is carrying it, so the limit reached is a person's capacity rather than the judgement *intolerable* hands down.

entries.definition: incapable of being tolerated or endured
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The same limit measured in duration - what cannot be lasted out, where *unbearable* is what cannot be held up under.

entries.definition: too extreme to bear
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Says exactly what *insufferable* says, and the difference is flatness rather than degree.

entries.definition: not able to be supported or defended
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Shifts the fault from what cannot be borne to what cannot be defended, so the weakness is in the thing's own standing rather than in anyone's strain.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Puts the unreasonableness first and lets the derision follow as a verdict, where *laughable* starts from the laugh.
examples: the absurd excuse that the dog ate his homework

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Informal and offhand, treating the thing as skewed out of true and waving it away rather than arguing with it.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the scorn in its own body: the thing is not merely open to derision but fit for nothing else.

entries.definition: devoid of good sense or judgment
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plain, unadorned charge that good sense or judgement is simply absent, with none of the mockery *ridiculous* invites.

entries.definition: ludicrous, foolish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Almost fond, taking the foolishness as entertainment rather than a fault, a long way from *idiotic*.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Hits hardest of these, aiming the derision squarely at whoever produced the thing rather than at the thing itself.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The lightest verdict here, since the derision it invites is a laugh, which can diminish a thing more thoroughly than an attack on it.
examples: a contribution so small as to be laughable

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Theatrical, full-blown absurdity, grander than *laughable* and past the point where argument is possible.
examples: it is ludicrous to call a cottage a mansion

entries.definition: devoid of intelligence or thought
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Nothing at all stands behind it, neither intelligence nor thought, a flatter and heavier charge than *foolish*'s bad judgement.

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Locates the failure in the sense itself, so nothing coherent is left to answer, where *absurd* still concedes a shape to reject.
examples: ask a nonsensical question and get a nonsensical answer

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and indignant, repudiating the absurdity out loud rather than merely laughing at it as *laughable* does.
examples: a preposterous attempt to turn back the pages of history

entries.definition: so unreasonable as to invite derision
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Blunt and immediate, the derision arriving without the argument *absurd* implies.
examples: her conceited assumption of universal interest in her rather dull children was ridiculous

entries.definition: ludicrous, foolish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest word here, foolish and ludicrous at a scale too small to be worth condemning.

entries.definition: devoid of intelligence or thought
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Names the emptiness as blankness rather than stupidity, the intelligence and thought simply not in evidence.

entries.definition: devoid of intelligence or thought
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal and colder than *mindless*, treating the absence of intelligence or thought as a settled quality of the thing.

entries.definition: ludicrous, foolish
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Foolishness with energy behind it, off-kilter and lively where *silly* is merely slight.
examples: some wacky plan for selling more books
